description: Sync emails from the Microsoft 365 mailboxes you choose, one document per email in each mailbox. Each email is restricted to its mailbox owner when Enforce ACL is on and the owner's address can be read.
opening: Sync emails from the Microsoft 365 mailboxes you select. Each email in each mailbox is one document, so a message received by two selected mailboxes is two documents. An email is grouped with the rest of its conversation in that mailbox.

With Enforce ACL on, an email can be read only by the owner of the mailbox it came from. Recipients do not get access through someone else's mailbox. `Mail.Read` gives the app every mailbox in your tenant unless you limit it in Exchange. Drafts, Junk Email, Deleted Items and a few other folders are not synced, and permanently deleted mail stays in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: Each email can be read only by the owner of the mailbox it was synced from. Recipients appear in the text and the graph, but get no access through another person's copy. To let a recipient find an email, select their mailbox too: their copy carries their own access.
permissions.identity: The mailbox address, in lower case.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot resolve a mailbox owner's address, the email is marked with a permission warning, which you can find with `additional_metadata.rbac_warning`.
notes: Shared and delegated mailbox access is not reflected. Only the mailbox's own address can read its emails.

connect.auth: Outlook uses a Microsoft Entra ID app registration with application permissions and a client secret. The same app can also back a Microsoft Teams connector.
connect.credentials_note: The form also shows `include_private_channels`. It is a Microsoft Teams setting and has no effect on mail.
connect.permissions_label: Microsoft Graph application permissions to grant

permissions.name: User.ReadBasic.All
permissions.text: lists mailboxes for you to select, and resolves senders and recipients to names and addresses.

permissions.name: Mail.Read
permissions.text: reads the mail of the selected mailboxes.

connect.permissions_note: `Mail.Read` grants the app every mailbox in the tenant. To limit it to the mailboxes you select, create an Exchange application access policy with `New-ApplicationAccessPolicy`, naming the app id and a group, with `RestrictAccess`. A selected mailbox outside the policy fails its sync with a message that names the policy.

steps.title: Register an app
steps.text: In Microsoft Entra ID, register an app and create a client secret. Copy the tenant id, the client id and the secret's Value.

steps.title: Grant permissions
steps.text: Add the Microsoft Graph application permissions above, not delegated ones, and grant admin consent.

steps.title: Limit mailbox access
steps.text: Optional. Create an Exchange application access policy so the app can read only the mailboxes you plan to select.

steps.title: Select mailboxes
steps.text: HydraDB lists the tenant's users as mailboxes. Select the mailboxes to sync.

steps.title: Rotate the secret
steps.text: Rotate the client secret before it expires.

connect.account: One connector reads the mailboxes you select in one Microsoft 365 tenant.

sync.first_sync: Each selected mailbox reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the mail in each selected mailbox whose last-modified time moved since the last sync.
sync.edits: An email moved to another folder or recategorised is read again and replaces its document.
sync.deletes: Mail moved to Deleted Items or Junk Email is replaced by a hidden stub only when it was received at or before the start of the time window that sync reads. With Enforce ACL on, nobody can read the stub. Other deleted mail, and mail deleted permanently, stays searchable in HydraDB.

documents.name: Emails
documents.one_document: One email in one mailbox. A message received by two selected mailboxes is two documents. Drafts are skipped.
documents.title: The subject, or `Email` and the Message-ID when there is no subject.
documents.text: The subject, the sender, the To and CC lines and the sent time, then the email's text with HTML stripped. When there is no text body, the preview is used, else the title. Bcc recipients are not in the text.
documents.date: When the email was received, else when it was sent, else when it was created.

attributes.name: from
attributes.text: The sender as `Name <address>`, written as the From line. The graph records the email as sent by that person.

attributes.name: to
attributes.text: The To recipients, written as the To line. The graph records each as a recipient.

attributes.name: cc
attributes.text: The CC recipients, written as the CC line. The graph records each as copied.

attributes.name: bcc
attributes.text: The Bcc recipients, present only on mail in the sender's own mailbox. The graph records each as a Bcc recipient. Not searchable.

attributes.name: sent_at
attributes.text: When the email was sent, written as the Date line. The result date when the received time is missing.

attributes.name: received_at
attributes.text: When the email was received. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the email was created. The result date only when the received and sent times are both missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.thread_id
attributes.text: The Outlook conversation id. Returns every email of one conversation, and groups the conversation's emails in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.mailbox_address
attributes.text: The address of the mailbox the email was synced from. Limits a query to one person's mail. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.mailbox_id
attributes.text: The Microsoft 365 user id of that mailbox. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The mail folder's id. Limits a query to one folder. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The mail folder's name. Limits a query to one folder by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `mail_folder`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.folder
attributes.text: The well-known folder name, such as `inbox`, `sentitems` or `archive`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_sent
attributes.text: `true` for mail in Sent Items. Keeps only mail the mailbox owner wrote. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.categories
attributes.text: The email's Outlook categories. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.has_attachments
attributes.text: `true` when the email has a non-inline attachment. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
attributes.text: Present when the mailbox owner's address could not be resolved. Finds such mail. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_deleted
attributes.text: `true` on the hidden stub that replaces deleted or junked mail. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's emails. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `outlook`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: mailbox
attributes.text: The address of the mailbox the email was synced from. Its owner is the only reader. Not searchable.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The same value as `from`.

attributes.name: reply_to
attributes.text: The Reply-To addresses.

attributes.name: message_id
attributes.text: The internet Message-ID, the same on every mailbox's copy of the email.

attributes.name: attachments
attributes.text: The names of non-inline attachments.

attributes.name: importance
attributes.text: `high` or `low`, when the email's importance is not normal.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the email was last modified. A change to it makes the next sync read the email again.

example_searches: What did Acme's procurement team email us about the renewal terms?
What is the latest message in the Q3 audit conversation?
Who was copied on the offer letter email to Jordan?

connections: Every email to its conversation in its mailbox, so the conversation's emails are kept together in time order.
No links to other tools. Copies of one email in two mailboxes stay separate documents.
people: The To, CC and Bcc recipients.
Reply-To addresses are not attached as people.

not_synced: Drafts, Outbox, Junk Email, Deleted Items, Conversation History and Clutter, and their subfolders.
Attachment types other than images, PDF and DOCX. Item and reference attachments are not downloaded.
Permanent deletions: purged mail stays in HydraDB.
